stack_version_constraints.libc: 0.2.186 direct declaration; already present in Cargo.lock transitively

issue_discussion_notes: Tauri issue signal: immediate child kill may not terminate spawned descendants.
Rust pipe Q&A signal: sequential stdout/stderr pipe reads can block when one pipe fills.
Pipe deadlock discussions support concurrent bounded reader threads and explicit cleanup.
community_signal_notes: Community sources were treated as failure-mode discovery only; implementation relies on official Rust/Unix/portable-pty APIs.

language_options.tradeoffs: Uses current owner of child processes and PTY handles; can set Unix process group and wait child directly; keeps packaging boundary small.
Could use Node process tooling but adds another runtime, more pipes, and larger installer surface.

language_decision_notes: The leaked resources are owned by Rust structs, so cleanup belongs in Rust Drop/finalize/dispose paths instead of renderer code or a sidecar.

architecture_options.reason: Easy to miss future cleanup paths and hard to test.

architecture_options.option: Centralized dispose/finalize helpers plus Drop guards
architecture_options.reason: Gives one lifecycle contract for cancel, timeout, store removal, and unexpected drop.

architecture_theory_sources: Rust ownership and Drop semantics from standard library docs
Unix process group semantics through CommandExt documentation
architecture_tradeoff_notes: Centralized cleanup adds small synchronous join grace, but bounds UI blocking to 250ms and avoids unbounded reader/process retention.
code_reference_notes: The existing code already used bounded output and reader threads; this change strengthens cleanup ownership rather than replacing the architecture.

folder_structure_options.option: New Rust module for process supervisor
folder_structure_options.reason: Current lib.rs already owns commands and stores; extracting a module would broaden blast radius.

folder_structure_options.option: Keep scoped helpers near session lifecycle code
folder_structure_options.reason: Smallest maintainable change for current source layout.

folder_structure_decision_notes: No source folders reshaped; specs and records use existing platform-desktop-app conventions.
folder_semantics_notes: Runtime lifecycle helpers remain in Tauri backend because they own OS handles.
maintainability_notes: Readiness tokens protect lifecycle primitives from accidental removal; future Windows process-tree cleanup can extend helper internals.
